data.name: Ganesha
data.gender_notes: Ganesha is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ganesha is the deity with the head of an elephant, the god of wisdom, the remover of obstacles, the deity honored at the start of any new venture or at the beginning of a journey. The name Ganesha carries the meaning “Elephant-headed god” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ganesha usually hope their child will grow to embody elephant-headed god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes wisdom, strength, and new beginnings.
data.etymology: Ganesha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Elephant-headed god.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ganesha total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Ganesha is renowned as the god of wisdom, knowledge, and the wisest of gods in Hinduism. He is regarded as the god of beginnings, prosperity, and the god of delivering good fortune and new beginnings. Ganesha's image is ubiquitous and visible as the mountain-sized icon at the entrances of temples, homes, and workplaces. He is revered as the patron of arts, sciences, and letters, and is worshipped not only by Hindus but also by Buddhists, Jains, and even some Sikhs. The festival of Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrated in September, is devoted to his worship and attracts millions of followers every year. The legend of Ganesha's elephant head begs the question, what seems like a hindrance can be transformed into an asset. This iconic image serves as a reminder that obstacles are opportunities, and with wisdom and a determined spirit, they can be overcome.
data.spiritual_significance: Ganesha is an embodiment of the infinite wisdom of the universe, and his elephant head represents the divine intelligence that unlocks the mysteries of existence. The soul (represented by the human form) and the intellect (represented by the elephant head) are inseparable in Ganesha. This amalgamation represents the highest potential of human consciousness. Ganesha's essence incorporates the energy of devotion, courage, power, and wisdom. He offers us the courage to overcome our weaknesses, the power to overcome our challenges, and the wisdom to navigate through our lives. Through the fulfillment of desire, we come closer to realizing our true nature—the pure consciousness that resides in every being. Worshiping Ganesha connects us with this divine energy and allows us to remove the inner obstacles, making way for a more meaningful and enlightened self.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ganesha, the elephant-headed god, symbolizes wisdom, new beginnings, and the removal of obstacles. He is the deity honored at the start of enterprises, rituals, and journeys, signifying his role as the remover of obstacles and the patron of success.

historical_references.reference: Ganesha is known as the god of wisdom and the remover of obstacles. He is the son of Shiva and Parvati. The story of his birth is recounted in the Shiva Purana. Parvati created Ganesha out of clay and brought him to life by giving him the life force of her own body. Later, when Shiva returned home, he was enraged to find this new son and ordered his warriors to attack him. Ganesha was able to fend them off with his vehicle, the mouse, and his elephant head, which Parvati had given him as a gift before sending him out into the world.

Ganesha is also known as the god of beginnings and the lord of obstacles, symbolized by his elephant head. He is depicted as having the head of an elephant, a large belly, and multiple arms, each holding various objects such as a goad, a noose, and a modak (a sweet rice cake). He is often worshipped as the deity who is invoked at the beginning of any new venture, as he is believed to remove obstacles and bring good luck. The reason for Ganesha's elephant head is a popular legend. One version of the story is that Parvati, angered by Shiva's neglect of her during meditation, created Ganesha and sent him to stop Shiva from entering their home while she bathed. When Shiva returned home, Ganesha refused to let him pass, and a battle ensued. Angered, Shiva beheaded Ganesha. When Parvati discovered what had happened, she was devastated and begged Shiva to bring her son back to life. Shiva agreed, but on one condition - that Ganesha would be given the head of the first creature he encountered on his journey back to life. Ganesha encountered an elephant, and so his head was replaced with that of an elephant.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu deity Ganesha, known for his elephant head and the remover of obstacles, has gained significant popularity and relevance in modern times across various platforms. In pop culture, Ganesha is often depicted in music, movies, and memes, reflecting his universal appeal and iconic status. In the social media sphere, Ganesha-themed content abounds, from hashtags like #GaneshChaturthi to digital art and stories shared during the festival. The music and entertainment industries have long celebrated Ganesha, with songs dedicated to him and films centered around his stories. Lastly, retail and merchandise industries have capitalized on the global appeal of Ganesha, selling everything from statues to clothing and accessories.
